title: Copy activity performance and scalability guide (Fabric Data Factory)

claims.text: The Copy activity runs on a serverless architecture that exposes parallelism at three distinct levels: control flow can launch many copy activities concurrently (for example inside a ForEach loop), each activity can scale its own compute via intelligent throughput optimization, and within one activity multiple threads read from the source and write to the destination in parallel.

Intelligent throughput optimization (ITO) is the Copy activity's compute-sizing lever: the service weighs CPU, memory, network allocation, and the expected cost of the run to pick a throughput level. It accepts the presets Auto, Standard, Balanced, and Maximum, or an explicit numeric value between 4 and 256.

Degree of copy parallelism is effectively a thread cap inside a single Copy activity: it bounds the maximum number of concurrent reader/writer threads, must be an integer of at least 1, and at run time the service may use fewer threads than the configured value when that yields better performance.

Parallel copy and intelligent throughput optimization are orthogonal settings: ITO sizes the compute resources for the run, while degree of parallelism controls thread fan-out, and by default the service chooses an optimal parallelism dynamically from the source-destination pair and the observed data pattern.

Because copy fully utilizes network bandwidth plus source and destination IOPS/bandwidth, achievable end-to-end throughput can be estimated as the minimum of three numbers: what the source store can serve, what the destination store can absorb, and the network bandwidth between them.

To scale ingestion beyond what one Copy activity delivers, fan out at the orchestration layer: drive multiple Copy activities in parallel from a ForEach loop, partitioning the workload (for example by table or file range) across iterations.

Explicitly lowering the degree of copy parallelism is the documented way to protect a fragile source or destination system: capping the thread count limits the concurrent load the copy places on the machines hosting the data stores.

Tuning copy throughput without first measuring the bottleneck is wasted effort: if the constraint is the source store's IOPS or the network path, raising intelligent throughput optimization or parallelism settings on the Copy activity cannot push throughput past that external limit.

Data Factory pipelines with Copy activity are Microsoft's recommended mechanism for large-scale one-time migrations (data lake or enterprise data warehouse into OneLake) and for high-volume recurring ingestion, on the grounds that the engine is serverless, performant at scale, and cost-effective.

The ITO presets trade cost against speed: Auto lets the service pick freely for the source-destination pair and data pattern, Standard stays within standard compute resources, Balanced weighs throughput against available compute, and Maximum applies all available compute resources to the run.
